BOS.head: The Bruins should be in control
BOS.body: Even though Boston may be without Pastrňák, the Bruins have been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately and have home-ice advantage. If the Canucks want to spoil it, start with a power play that gets going.

VAN.body: Even though Boston may be without Pastrňák, the Bruins have been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately and have home-ice advantage. The Canucks’ best hope is a power play that gets going, plus a big night from Leevi Meriläinen.

story.head: The Bruins are likely to drive the play
paras: The Bruins (15-9-1) lost 3-1 to Toronto on Friday, and the Canucks are on a three-game losing streak. Going in, the Canucks are last in the NHL and the Bruins fifth in the Atlantic (tied for 14th in the NHL).

The Canucks haven’t played well, but their record (.232) is worse than their play: their chances are worth about .343, and their goaltending has held them back. The Bruins’ record (.620) is about what their chances are worth.

The Canucks pick their shots (lowest), have had shaky goaltending (32nd) and have a leaky penalty kill (32nd). The Bruins, by contrast, have had some of the best goaltending in the league (2nd). Vancouver has allowed 4.43 goals a game, the most in the league. As for the Bruins, they leave the shooting to their forwards (2nd lowest) and sit back rather than chase on the forecheck (2nd lowest). Boston has allowed 2.72 goals a game, the fourth fewest in the league. The Bruins have the edge over the Canucks on shot suppression. Beyond that, the Bruins could find some good looks against the Canucks, who give up plenty of them.

Brock Boeser (8 G / 20 A / 28 P in 28 GP) is carrying the Canucks’ offense, and Jake DeBrusk (9 G / 6 A / 15 P in 26 GP) has a team-high nine goals. For the Bruins, Elias Lindholm (11 G / 11 A / 22 P in 25 GP) leads the way in scoring, with four goals in six games against Vancouver since 2023-24. Morgan Geekie (6 G / 15 A / 21 P in 25 GP) isn’t far behind.
Leevi Meriläinen (4-12-1 / .883 SV% in 18 GS) will likely start for Vancouver, and Jeremy Swayman (11-7-1 / .899 SV% in 19 GS) for Boston.
The Bruins usually control more of the chances than the Canucks do.

items.text: The Canucks are newly without Filip Chytil, have been without Elias Pettersson (#40) since Nov 19, and have had to make do without Thatcher Demko all season. Leevi Meriläinen is expected to start.
The Bruins are newly without David Pastrňák, and have been without Michael Eyssimont and James Hagens for several games.
JJ Peterka has five goals on chances worth about 7.4 goals, well below what his finishing usually turns chances into. If the chances keep coming, so should the goals.
Jake DeBrusk is two goals from 200.
